items.title: Time
items.best_for: fashion boutiques, hair salons, dance and skating schools, family businesses, personal trainers
items.idea: Fashion boutique: a childhood dress-up photo, then the owner in this season’s collection
ideas: Fashion boutique: a childhood dress-up photo, then the owner in this season’s collection
Family business: the founder’s first day, then the team today
Dance school: a student’s first recital, then their latest performance
Personal trainer: a client’s day one, then the same move today
items.about: This is the “then and now” sound of the month. Creators start with a childhood photo, then cut to who they are today, with a line like “I’ve loved fashion since I came out the womb.” One skater used it for a comeback at 50, and it passed 130K plays.

items.title: Last Christmas
items.best_for: holiday events and attractions, tourism boards, photo studios, bars and restaurants, retail stores
items.idea: Holiday attraction: the lights switching on for the first night, from one bulb to the whole display
ideas: Holiday attraction: the lights switching on for the first night, from one bulb to the whole display
Photo studio: friends in the holiday photo booth, one pose per beat
Bar: the first holiday cocktail menu of the year, poured and garnished
Retail store: the front window going from fall to full Christmas
items.about: The “Christmas music is allowed now” sound. Ten of the Reels on its page went up between November 13 and 16. Tourism brands are already on it: Arizona’s tourism account used it to announce a million-light holiday show.

items.title: It's Beginning to Look a Lot like Christmas
items.best_for: bakeries, home decor stores, interior designers, real estate agents, luxury retail
items.idea: Bakery: a plain tray of brownies turned into Christmas trees, step by step
ideas: Bakery: a plain tray of brownies turned into Christmas trees, step by step
Home decor store: an empty shelf to a full holiday display in five cuts
Real estate agent: a listing staged for the holidays, front door to living room
Interior designer: one room, before and after holiday styling
items.about: The title does the work here. It’s the sound for “the decorations are going up” Reels, from a brand-new house dressed for Christmas (2.5M plays) to the holiday decor at Dior’s Paris flagship. Food creators are using it too, like a Christmas brownie tutorial that passed 247K plays.

items.title: Christmas Market
items.best_for: gift shops, home decor brands, coffee shops, photo studios, hotels
items.idea: Gift shop: a slow walk past every holiday shelf, ending at the till
ideas: Gift shop: a slow walk past every holiday shelf, ending at the till
Coffee shop: the holiday drink built layer by layer, with the recipe on screen
Photo studio: the holiday set, lit up, with your hourly rate on screen
Hotel: the lobby tree, the fireplace, and a room turned down for the night
items.about: A soft instrumental that went from 72K to 89K Reels in three days. Shops and home creators use it for slow holiday corners: a coffee bar, a decorated kitchen, a store in full Christmas mode. Many end with “comment SHOP” for a link.

items.title: November
items.best_for: cafes and matcha bars, outdoor and swim brands, plant shops, wellness coaches, local tourism
items.idea: Matcha bar: a whisked matcha on a grey afternoon, steam rising
ideas: Matcha bar: a whisked matcha on a grey afternoon, steam rising
Swim brand: a cold-water dip, from the shiver to the smile
Plant shop: winter care for one plant, in three quiet shots
Wellness coach: a slow November morning routine, one habit per clip
items.about: The month’s own background track. It’s used for November photo dumps, colder-weather walks, and calm reflection clips. Kevin Bacon used it for a November dip in the Irish Sea (574K plays).

items.title: Coming Up Roses
items.best_for: small business owners, florists, wedding photographers, cafes, life and career coaches
items.idea: Small business: a year of tiny wins, from the first order to this week’s packing table
ideas: Small business: a year of tiny wins, from the first order to this week’s packing table
Florist: a week in the shop, one bouquet per beat
Wedding photographer: favorite candid moments from this season’s weddings
Coach: “you’ve done more than you think” with client wins on screen
items.about: It went from 49K to 116K Reels in under three weeks. The format is “silly little life”: fast cuts of small, happy moments. One creator shared her template, and that Reel passed 837K plays. Others use it for “you’ve done more than you think” messages.

items.title: Stop The Wedding!
items.best_for: skincare and beauty brands, bakeries, bridal shops, event planners, gift shops
items.idea: Skincare brand: “stop the wedding, our holiday bundle just dropped”
ideas: Skincare brand: “stop the wedding, our holiday bundle just dropped”
Bakery: an objection mid-ceremony because the cake hasn’t been tasted yet
Bridal shop: a bride stopping the try-on because she found “the one” dress
Gift shop: a giveaway, “tag the friend who would stop the wedding”
items.about: It’s #4 on Spotify in the U.S., and its Reel count more than doubled in under three weeks. The hook is dramatic: “stop the wedding, but…” followed by something small or funny. Brands are using it for giveaways, like a skincare bundle with @bev.skin.

items.title: I Knew It, I Knew You
items.best_for: coffee shops, family photographers, farms and farm shops, travel and lifestyle brands, toy stores
items.idea: Coffee shop: the morning ritual, from the first pour to the first sip
ideas: Coffee shop: the morning ritual, from the first pour to the first sip
Family photographer: a family session, ending on one candid laugh
Farm shop: a couple running the farm, one chore per beat
Toy store: two staff back to back, then a dance among the shelves
items.about: Taylor Swift’s song from Toy Story 5 has turned into a soft “this is my life” sound. Couples, families, and small lifestyle brands set it under everyday moments. The other format is a back-to-back bump that breaks into a coordinated dance.

items.title: BEAUTY AND A BEAT X COLA (ALTÉGO MIX)
items.best_for: lash and nail artists, fitness brands, cheer and dance teams, motorbike and car shops, videographers
items.idea: Lash artist: a new set revealed in three angles, one per beat drop
ideas: Lash artist: a new set revealed in three angles, one per beat drop
Fitness brand: a day of meals with your Black Friday code on screen
Dance team: a teaser of the show, cut before the big moment
Videographer: your best transitions of the year in 15 seconds
items.about: A high-energy mashup for “look at this” reveals. Lash artists use it for set reveals, and a fitness creator used it to share a Black Friday discount code. It’s a strong fit for Black Friday teasers this week.

items.title: Mr. Brightside
items.best_for: fitness studios, bars and pubs, high school and local sports teams, vintage stores, music venues
items.idea: Fitness studio: one class, set to the build, ending on the chorus
ideas: Fitness studio: one class, set to the build, ending on the chorus
Bar: throwback night, from the first round to the singalong
Sports team: the season so far, ending on the record
Vintage store: 2000s fits, one per beat
items.about: The millennial anthem is back in the U.S. Spotify top 15. Creators use it for “going back to our roots” throwbacks and high-energy workouts. A jump-rope studio’s Reel passed 124K plays.

items.title: The Blue Danube Waltz
items.best_for: pilates and yoga studios, cleaning services, pet groomers, tailors and dressmakers, boutiques
items.idea: Pilates studio: resetting the reformers after class, filmed like a waltz
ideas: Pilates studio: resetting the reformers after class, filmed like a waltz
Cleaning service: a spotless finish, one graceful wipe at a time
Pet groomer: a fluffy dog’s blow-dry, played completely straight
Boutique: a new-arrivals try-on, “for absolutely no reason”
items.about: The joke is treating something ordinary like a grand ballet. A dressmaker’s battle with an apple slicer passed 1.2M plays, and a pilates instructor used it for a studio clean-up. Later also lists it for playful “every girl for absolutely no reason” hauls.

analysis.week_summary: 'Housewife' by Tate McRae leads Instagram Reels this week (Heat 86). 1 seasonal or returning sounds are back (All I Want for Christmas Is You). The best opportunity right now is 'Housewife': high heat and not yet crowded.
key_takeaways: Reels × Ireland crossover: 'Housewife' (#6 in Ireland), 'Stop the Wedding!' (#1 in Ireland), 'Last Christmas' (#5 in Ireland). These are the strongest local signals.
6 of 14 tracked sounds are rising: move early on 'Stop the Wedding!', 'Coming Up Roses', 'November'.
'It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas' already has 1M+ reels, so you need a strong hook to stand out.
Most major-label songs may be blocked for Business accounts: reuse the same formats with original audio or a voiceover.
analysis.ireland_signal: Also charting in Ireland: Housewife (#6), Stop the Wedding! (#1), Last Christmas (#5). Irish acts in the top 20: Kingfishr, Fontaines D.C.. Good material for Irish-pride content.
